name: shimmer-loader

frames.best_why: Frame 3 shows all three bars at 83% with distinct cycling labels and token counts.

tagline: Three purple terminal progress bars shimmer and tick up with percent and tokens.
summary: A stack of monospace progress bars that a purple shimmer sweeps across while the labels cycle and the percentages and token counts climb, then restart from zero when finished.
appearance: On a black panel, three stacked strips of purple gradient cells each hold a centred monospace label and percentage. A bright violet shimmer band moves across each strip, a small purple glyph sits at the left and a dim '0.1k' style token count at the right.
behaviour: Each bar counts up from zero to 100% over a few seconds while the shimmer sweeps and the label word changes in stages. When a bar completes it restarts from zero, so the three strips loop continuously.
demo_content: Three loaders labelled Analysing, Booting or Initializing, and Syncing or Onboarding, with token targets.
use_when: An AI or devtool screen wants a distinctive charging-up indicator with labels and token figures instead of a plain bar.
avoid_when: It loops on its own and reports fake progress, so it must not stand in for a real measured task or a cancel control.
customise: Labels, icon glyphs, duration, token target, whether percent shows, font size, cell padding and text colour are props; the purple gradient maths is fixed in the source.
weight_why: A requestAnimationFrame loop recolours every cell of three strips forty times a second.

a11y.note: There is no progressbar role or live value, so screen readers get the label text but not the percentage, and the loop ignores reduced motion.

issues: The token counter at the right is a very dim purple and is barely readable.
polish_why: A distinctive terminal look with a smooth shimmer; the token counter is too faint to read.
title: Shimmer Loader
